phases.title: Project foundation
phases.goal: Set a truthful, enforceable development contract before claiming new AI capability.

acceptance.criterion: Navigation, scope, evidence vocabulary and ownership roles are documented; the original README image is preserved byte-for-byte.
acceptance.verification: Repository inspection, link checks and image checksum

acceptance.criterion: Offline roadmap validation and its positive/negative unit tests pass without a GPU toolchain.
acceptance.verification: python3 ci/project/check_project.py; python3 -m unittest discover -s ci/project -p 'test_*.py'

acceptance.criterion: Independent reviews are resolved and the delivered commit is verified on the intended repository and branch.
acceptance.verification: Review ledger, git diff and GitHub branch readback

phases.title: Reproducible baseline
phases.goal: Reproduce inherited capabilities on pinned configurations; inherited source is not a new measurement.

acceptance.criterion: A clean checkout reproduces a pinned toolchain, submodules, generated configuration and build with full command provenance.
acceptance.verification: Clean-room build log and tool/config hashes

acceptance.criterion: Native FP16/BF16 tensor GEMM and supported small attention cases pass CPU-reference checks on SimX and native rtlsim; DPI runs are separately labelled.
acceptance.verification: Named existing catalog cases, raw logs, reference tolerances and backend record

acceptance.criterion: Full AFU integration is exercised on XRT hardware emulation where available; unavailable integration is explicitly blocked, never passed.
acceptance.verification: XRT hw_emu report including DMA, launch and completion

phases.title: Tensor numerical contract
phases.goal: Define and prove the exact arithmetic behavior of the first supported AI configuration.

acceptance.criterion: Versioned format/backend contracts specify rounding, accumulation, exceptional values, overflow, underflow and tolerances before evaluation.
acceptance.verification: Reviewed numeric contract and deterministic fixture manifest

acceptance.criterion: Native FP16/BF16-to-FP32 arithmetic passes normal, edge, cancellation and layout tests; unsupported formats fail explicitly.
acceptance.verification: Reference comparisons on SimX and native RTL, not a DPI replacement

acceptance.criterion: WGMMA synchronization, metadata, multi-warp and backpressure cases preserve correctness with no unexplained model divergence.
acceptance.verification: Concurrency tests and model-parity evidence or documented applicability limits

phases.title: AI operator library
phases.goal: Expose stable native AI operators without requiring a new HIP toolchain.

acceptance.criterion: A versioned operator manifest covers matmul/GEMV, reductions, softmax, normalization, activations, layout/casts and attention with supported dtype/shape/layout ranges.
acceptance.verification: Operator manifest, ABI review and explicit unsupported-operation tests

acceptance.criterion: Every supported operator passes deterministic and edge-case CPU-reference checks through real device launches; CPU fallback is explicit and separately reported.
acceptance.verification: Per-operator numerical reports and dispatch traces on SimX/native RTL

acceptance.criterion: Buffer bounds, queue/event lifetimes, transfer errors and repeated allocation/free behavior pass host integration tests.
acceptance.verification: Negative tests and leak/resource accounting logs

phases.title: Tiny-model inference
phases.goal: Execute a fixed, redistributable tiny model end-to-end through native AI operators.

acceptance.criterion: Model, tokenizer if needed, weights or generator, seeds, shapes and licenses are fixed and reproducible without large proprietary downloads.
acceptance.verification: Small fixture manifest with hashes and license/provenance

acceptance.criterion: An end-to-end tiny transformer or equivalently specified network matches its frozen CPU reference, with layer-level and final-output tolerances locked before the run.
acceptance.verification: Deterministic native-runtime model report and intermediate comparisons

acceptance.criterion: Device traces prove the declared accelerated operators ran on Vortex; transfer costs and any allowed host work are reported separately.
acceptance.verification: Dispatch and transfer traces plus latency breakdown

phases.title: Python and framework integration
phases.goal: Let Python users invoke the proven runtime while clearly separating a custom-op bridge from a full device backend.

acceptance.criterion: A thin Python binding supports the declared dtypes, shapes, strides, lifetimes and explicit errors; package installation works in a clean environment.
acceptance.verification: Binding tests, packaging smoke and dependency lock/provenance

acceptance.criterion: A supported PyTorch custom-op path reproduces the native tiny-model result without silent CPU fallback or unsupported autograd claims.
acceptance.verification: Framework-to-device trace and numerical comparison

acceptance.criterion: The compatibility matrix names tested framework versions, operators and limitations; CUDA binary compatibility is not implied.
acceptance.verification: Versioned matrix and failure-mode tests

phases.title: Memory and performance scaling
phases.goal: Measure and improve useful work per second, byte and joule without confusing simulation with physical speed.

acceptance.criterion: A frozen workload/configuration suite records cycles, transfers, cache/local-memory use and computation counts with warm-up and repeat policy.
acceptance.verification: Reproducible benchmark manifests, raw samples and analysis

acceptance.criterion: Each optimization preserves numeric contracts and inherited performance gates; native RTL and SimX changes remain synchronized.
acceptance.verification: Before/after data, correctness and applicable parity/gate results

acceptance.criterion: The chosen scale/configuration fits explicit resource and timing budgets; predicted and measured quantities are separated.
acceptance.verification: Synthesis/resource reports and documented target budget

phases.title: Physical FPGA prototype
phases.goal: Prove real compute, real external DRAM and real host transfers on one selected supported board.

acceptance.criterion: A board/platform/tool license decision is recorded; firmware, memory map, toolchain, bitstream hash and achieved clock are pinned.
acceptance.verification: Board readiness record and reproducible implementation report

acceptance.criterion: Physical hardware (not hw_emu) passes DMA, bank/address boundary, tensor, attention and the tiny-model tests against frozen references.
acceptance.verification: XRT --driver=xrt --target=hw with a matching TARGET=hw bitstream, or equivalent physical-board logs with device identity

acceptance.criterion: A one-hour initial soak completes with no unexplained numerical, transfer or reset errors; throughput, power and temperature are measured or explicitly unavailable.
acceptance.verification: Timestamped soak and telemetry report; failures block exit

phases.title: Reliability and release hardening
phases.goal: Turn a proven prototype into a reproducible, supportable experimental release.

acceptance.criterion: Error propagation, resource exhaustion, malformed requests, reset/recovery and memory isolation are tested against an explicit threat/failure model.
acceptance.verification: Fault-injection results and resolved critical findings

acceptance.criterion: A 24-hour physical soak passes the declared workload matrix with zero unexplained errors; known limitations are published.
acceptance.verification: Raw soak logs, telemetry and issue disposition

acceptance.criterion: Versioned installation artifacts, source/license inventory, compatibility matrix and release evidence are reproducible and reviewed.
acceptance.verification: Clean install/reproduction report and signed-off experimental release checklist

phases.title: Training and multi-device research
phases.goal: Investigate training and cooperating accelerators as separately demonstrated capabilities.

acceptance.criterion: A small training workload matches reference gradients and convergence under predeclared precision and optimizer settings.
acceptance.verification: Training numerical and convergence evidence

acceptance.criterion: Two-device transport and collectives pass correctness, ordering, failure and recovery tests before any scaling claim.
acceptance.verification: Physical topology and collective-test report

acceptance.criterion: Scaling and communication costs are measured on declared hardware; unsupported NVLink/CUDA equivalence claims are absent.
acceptance.verification: Single/multi-device comparative measurements

phases.title: ASIC feasibility and sign-off planning
phases.goal: Make an evidence-backed go/no-go decision for a bounded inference ASIC; training research is not a prerequisite.

acceptance.criterion: Foundry/PDK, SRAM macros, PCIe and memory controller/PHY IP, packaging and tool licenses have qualified owners and written availability/cost evidence.
acceptance.verification: Reviewed feasibility package and dependency register

acceptance.criterion: The target configuration has complete physical-design, DFT, timing, power-integrity and verification plans with no black-box memory assumptions presented as sign-off.
acceptance.verification: PPA reports labelled as estimates plus qualified sign-off checklist

acceptance.criterion: Budget, schedule, procurement, ownership and external partners are explicitly approved before tapeout commitments.
acceptance.verification: Recorded human go/no-go approval; no automated spending

phases.title: Funded silicon realization and bring-up
phases.goal: Fabricate and validate a funded design only after actual manufacturing sign-off.

acceptance.criterion: Foundry-qualified verification, DFT and physical sign-off complete with reviewed exceptions and an explicitly approved manufacturing release.
acceptance.verification: Sign-off reports and authorized tapeout record

acceptance.criterion: Packaged silicon and its board pass power/clock/reset, memory training, host enumeration, DMA and core/tensor tests.
acceptance.verification: Lab measurements with device/board revisions and failure records

acceptance.criterion: The frozen model suite runs on silicon; measured frequency, capacity, performance, power and yield limits are published honestly.
acceptance.verification: Silicon acceptance report and release decision
